origin.description: Put a backslash in front of every character that is special to the regular-expression engine.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A character vector, or another vector that can be coerced to character.

origin.details: The metacharacters are . ^ $ \ | * + ? { } [ ] ( ). A missing string stays missing. Names on string are copied. NULL is an empty character vector.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as string.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

translation.details: The replacement is the ICU form of a literal backslash plus the captured character. The result is a list. Names on the input are copied.
translation.value: A list of strings. A missing string is NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.escape import str_escape
print("str_escape(\".\") returns " + str_escape(".")[0] + ".")
